quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending soon.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means two things: the protected left turn is ending, and you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks while moving with other vehicles?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Before crossing railroad tracks, make sure your entire vehicle will fit on the other side.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road fast.
Ease off the gas, slow down, then gradually steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease off the gas, slow down, then gradually steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the road, stay calm. Take your foot off the gas and keep both hands on the wheel. Slow down and carefully steer back onto the road. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in school zones?

options.text: 10 mph
15 mph
25 mph
45 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 15 miles per hour. Drive slowly and carefully in areas where children may be present.

questions.question: How does increasing your speed affect your vision?

options.text: It improves your field of vision.
It reduces your field of vision.
It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
It has no effect on your vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces your field of vision.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. At higher speeds, you can see less around you, so you must pay close attention to potential hazards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. Do not turn right at an intersection displaying this sign.

questions.question: What should you do if your wheels drop off the road edge?

options.text: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the road when safe.
Turn back onto the road immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not try to turn back onto the road immediately. Instead, reduce speed, check for traffic, and gradually steer back when it is safe.

questions.question: You have a minor collision with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: If there are no injuries or deaths and you can do so safely, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane after a collision.

questions.question: Is night driving more or less dangerous than day driving?

options.text: Less dangerous.
Just as dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see, headlights can temporarily blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: Can you pass another vehicle when there are double solid yellow lines?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle in either direction may cross the center line to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: What does the posted speed limit show?

options.text: Only a suggested driving speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The highest safe speed when conditions are ideal.
The highest safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: The speed limit shows the highest legal speed for that road under ideal conditions. You may need to drive slower when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, stop completely. Do not proceed until the lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn. Make sure no children are crossing before you move.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before passing and make sure no traffic is coming toward you.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before passing left.
When passing, see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing: signal at least 100 feet ahead, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots, and wait to see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system can cause:

options.text: Hearing loss.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: A leaky exhaust system allows harmful fumes to enter the passenger area. Fix exhaust leaks immediately to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to be sure it is safe.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when signals flash. Watch for a lowered gate or an oncoming train.

questions.question: You can help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Driving at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed and signal your turns and lane changes ahead of time to help the driver behind you maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you plan to enter. Be ready to stop, but you may go if there is no conflicting traffic.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Stopping too much.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and your car slides on a thin layer of water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Keep driving at your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and be ready to stop. Follow the posted speed limits. Watch for workers and changing conditions.

questions.question: Which of these statements is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your driving ability, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. are allowed.
A steep hill is ahead.
A truck stop is ahead.
No trucks are allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: To reduce the effects of headlight glare at night, you should look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look toward the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.
